content.title: Nearby Partner Projects
content.summary: The article outlines several significant projects near Arvada that are not managed by the City, including the environmentally sustainable Golden Tech Center, the Colorado Mountain Rail transportation initiative, the Foothills Regional Housing Project aimed at affordable housing, and the Quantum COmmons development focused on advancing the quantum industry. Additionally, it mentions the closure of 21 schools by Jefferson County and the ongoing evaluation of future uses for those properties. Each project includes links for further updates and community engagement opportunities.
content.body:
This page provides information about high visibility and high interest projects or developments in or near Arvada that are not managed by the City. Links to the official sources are included so you can access information and updates directly.

1. [Golden Tech Center](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_0)

#### [Golden Tech Center](https://goldentechctr.com/)

- Brief Description: A proposed environmentally sustainable technology center on land (unincorporated Jefferson County) zoned for light industrial usage since the 1950s. The development will address view corridors, noise, sustainability, and community impacts given its proximity to residential areas.
- Location: McIntyre Street, Jefferson County
- City Involvement: provided feedback/requests to Jefferson County during the development proposal process.
- [Get Updates: Golden Tech Center website](https://goldentechctr.com/)

1. [Colorado Mountain Rail](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_1)

#### [Colorado Mountain Rail](https://www.codot.gov/projects/coloradomountainrail) (CDOT)

- Brief Description: CDOT’s initiative to enhance transportation using existing rail infrastructure, connecting mountain regions with urban centers and recreation hubs.
- Location: Central Rocky Mountains with passenger stops, including Arvada
- City Involvement: Arvada will notify the community about engagement opportunities presented by CDOT
- [Get Updates: Visit CDOT’s Colorado Mountain Rail page](https://www.codot.gov/projects/coloradomountainrail)

1. [Foothills Regional Housing](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_2)

#### [Foothills Regional Housing Project](https://www.foothillsrh.org/)

- Brief Description: An affordable housing project on 11.13 acres previously owned by the State, featuring seven unused buildings that have been abandoned since the 1970s. The site will be redeveloped for community benefit.
- Location: Ridge Road (54th Avenue and Miller Street), Wheat Ridge
- City Involvement: Arvada will notify the community about engagement opportunities presented by the City of Wheat Ridge and Foothills Regional Housing
- Get Updates: - [What’s Up Wheat Ridge Affordable Housing project page](https://whatsupwheatridge.com/housing) and [Foothills Regional Housing Website](https://www.foothillsrh.org/)

1. [Quantum COmmons](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_3)

#### [Quantum COmmons](https://electrical.mines.edu/copy-of-dr-yamuna-phal-awarded-nasa-grant-for-innovative-chiroptical-image/) (Colorado School of Mines)

- Brief Description: A 70-acre development designed to accelerate growth in the quantum industry and workforce. Spearheaded by the Colorado School of Mines, Elevate Quantum partners, and investments from State and Federal programs.
- Location: Between Indiana and Highway 93 along Highway 72, Arvada
- Time Frame: Groundbreaking began in 2024
- City Involvement: Arvada is involved through the Bloomberg Project and other partnerships
- [Get Updates: Colorado School of Mines/Quantum Commons Project](https://electrical.mines.edu/copy-of-dr-yamuna-phal-awarded-nasa-grant-for-innovative-chiroptical-image/)

1. [Jeffco Public Schools - Closed Schools Property Updates](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_4)

#### [Closures and Future Property Use](https://www.jeffcopublicschools.org/services/facilities/boundary-study)

- Brief Description: Jefferson County closed 21 schools between the 2020-21 and 2023-24 school years to address declining enrollment across Jefferson County. Jeffco is now in the process of determining the best use for those properties.
- Location: Multiple Jefferson County locations, including Arvada
- City Involvement: No
- [Learn about the Jeffco Public Schools Boundary Study](https://www.jeffcopublicschools.org/services/facilities/boundary-study)
- [Learn about the property status of the closed schools](https://www.jeffcopublicschools.org/services/facilities/property-disposition), which includes a [spreadsheet listing each school property](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vT5B66HsRiXsSIkpUFZcKiuEOAmZp1ORaAoZcTu5ydQZiK68g5xvhyhPy_tI8yttz6EN32H7TzmTDab/pub?start=false&loop=false&delayms=3000&slide=id.g29f83a9d6da_0_66)

1. [Adams County Safety Plan](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_5)

#### [Adams County Comprehensive Safety Action Plan](https://fhu.mysocialpinpoint.com/adams-county-comprehensive-safety-action-plan)

- Brief Description: A comprehensive transportation plan to address connectivity and mobility throughout Adams County.
- Location: Regional impacts near Arvada’s boundaries
- City Involvement: The City is providing requested transportation data and sharing opportunities for community feedback
- [Get Updates: Adams County Government Transportation page](https://fhu.mysocialpinpoint.com/adams-county-comprehensive-safety-action-plan)

1. [Gross Reservoir](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_6)

#### [Gross Reservoir Expansion Project](https://www.denverwater.org/grossreservoir/about-the-project/what-is-the-gross-reservoir-expansion-project)

- Brief Description: A Denver Water project to expand Gross Reservoir to address water storage needs for the growing region.
- Location: Gross Reservoir, Boulder County
- City Involvement: The City is a funding partner and will receive additional water supply from the project when complete
- [Get Updates: Visit Denver Water’s Gross Reservoir Project page](https://www.denverwater.org/grossreservoir/about-the-project/what-is-the-gross-reservoir-expansion-project)

1. [Jefferson County Public Library - Olde Town Redesign and NW Arvada New Build](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_7)

#### Jefferson County Public Library [Olde Town Redesign](https://jeffcolibrary.org/arvada-redesign/) & [Northwest Arvada New Build](https://jeffcolibrary.org/northwest-county/)

- Brief Description: Planned updates and developments to enhance library services in Jefferson County, including two locations impacting Arvada residents: Olde Town Library and Northwest Arvada.
- Location: Olde Town Arvada and Northwest Arvada locations
- City Involvement: Both projects will go through the City's development review process
- Get Updates: Visit Jeffco Public Library projects [Olde Town Redesign](https://jeffcolibrary.org/arvada-redesign/) & [Northwest Arvada New Build](https://jeffcolibrary.org/northwest-county/)

1. [Jefferson Parkway](#tab9043cec4-7b90-487d-9d98-2842ae576c30_8)

#### [Jefferson Parkway Construction](https://www.jpphauthority.org/)

- Brief Description: A proposed toll road designed to complete the metro Denver beltway
- Location: Northwest of Arvada, primarily in Jefferson County
- City Involvement: Arvada is a partner in an intergovernmental agreement with Jefferson County
- [Get Updates: Visit the Jefferson Parkway Public Highway Authority website](https://www.jpphauthority.org/)

## City-run Projects

Looking for projects that are led by the City of Arvada? Following are links to City project pages.

- [**Public Improvement Projects**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/612/Public-Improvement-Projects). The public improvement projects page includes a [City Construction Projects map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=834e165e7864450b9796460f9836b055).
- [**Park Projects**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/519/Park-Projects). The park projects page includes a City of Arvada Park Projects map. You can view the location, brief description and link to more info for each project.
- [**Development in Arvada**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1394/Active-Development-Projects). The development in Arvada page provides a map, so you can view a description and the location of residential and commercial development projects being processed by the City.
- [**Plan Arvada**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/304/Plan-Arvada-Current-Long-Range-Plans). The Plan Arvada page provides an overview of the City's current and long range plans related to Budget, Development, Sustainability, Transportation and Arts and Culture.

### Stay Informed

For updates on City-run projects and other information, visit the [Subscribe, Follow, Stay Informed](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1356/Subscribe-Follow-Stay-Informed) page.

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=109)

[Does the City hire the contractors for development projects?](#)
:   No. Developers hire their own contractors. The City's role is to review plans, issue permits, and inspect work to make sure it meets our standards—but we don't select or manage construction crews.

[If something looks wrong with a construction project, does that mean the City approved it?](#)
:   Not necessarily. When our inspectors find work that doesn't meet standards, we require contractors to fix it before moving forward. What might look like delays or repeated work is often the inspection process doing exactly what it's supposed to do.

[Is all the road work in my area a City project?](#)
:   Not always. Several state highways run through Arvada, including portions of W. 64th Avenue, Highway 72 and Highway 93. The Colorado Department of Transportation (**CDOT**) is responsible for approving and inspecting work on those roads. The City inspects utilities or infrastructure that we maintain, like a water line that runs under a CDOT road. More information about City Projects are available on the [Public Improvement Projects page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/612/Public-Improvement-Projects).

    **Key term: CDOT**

    The Colorado Department of Transportation, the state agency responsible for Colorado's highway system. CDOT manages construction and maintenance on state highways, which is separate from the City's authority over local roads.

[Can the City stop or slow down a development project if residents don't want it?](#)
:   When a development proposal meets **zoning** requirements and **code standards**, the City is legally required to approve it. We can shape how development happens through our standards, but we can't block projects that meet the rules.

    **Key term: Zoning**

    The set of rules that determines how land in a specific area can be used—for example, whether a property can be used for single-family homes, apartments, retail, or commercial businesses. Zoning also regulates things like building height, lot size, and how far a building must be set back from the street. The City's zoning map and regulations are part of the [Land Development Code](https://www.arvadaco.gov/179/Land-Development-Code).

    **Key term: Code standards**

    The rules and regulations that govern how buildings and infrastructure must be designed and constructed. These include building codes (structural safety, fire protection, plumbing, electrical), the land development code (site layout, parking, landscaping, stormwater), and engineering standards for roads and utilities.

[Why wasn't I told about a new development before construction started?](#)
:   Development projects go through a **public review process** that includes notification to nearby residents and opportunities to provide input. However, we know it can be hard to keep track of everything happening in a growing area. You can stay up to date by visiting the City's Active Development Projects page and clicking on the [Developments Under Review Map](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1394/Active-Development-Projects).

    **Key term: Public Review Process**

    The steps a development proposal goes through before it's approved, which may include neighborhood meetings, public hearings before the Planning Commission or City Council, and written notice mailed to nearby property owners. The specific steps depend on the type of project.

[Why is construction taking so long?](#)
:   Large developments happen in **phases** over months or years. Weather, supply chain issues, inspection requirements, and financing all affect timelines. What looks like stalled progress is often part of a planned sequence.

    **Key term: Phasing**

    The practice of building a large development in stages rather than all at once. Each phase typically includes its own set of homes, roads, and utility connections and must pass inspections before the next phase begins.

[Why didn't the City build the roads before allowing the development?](#)
:   Developers are typically required to build or pay for **infrastructure improvements**—like roads, water lines, and drainage—as part of their projects. The timing depends on development phasing and construction sequencing.

    **Key term: Infrastructure improvements**

    The roads, water lines, sewer lines, stormwater drainage, sidewalks, and other public systems that are built or upgraded to support new development. Developers are often required to fund or construct these improvements as a condition of their project approval.

[Shouldn't construction traffic be kept off residential streets?](#)
:   The City works with developers on traffic management plans, but construction vehicles often need to use public roads to access job sites. If you have specific concerns about safety or road damage from construction traffic, please reach out through [Ask Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/898/Report-a-Problem-or-Ask-a-Question).

[Will traffic go back to normal once construction is done?](#)
:   New construction or development doesn't always mean more traffic but changes in traffic patterns do happen over time. When any development is proposed within the City of Arvada, City staff review and approve that development. This process includes reviewing traffic impact studies that assess the current and future projected traffic in the area. This process identifies improvements that are needed when the development is built, as well as future changes that may need to be implemented as more homes and businesses are added to the area. The City also evaluates traffic on an ongoing basis to ensure we have the most efficient, effective and safe traffic control systems at each unique intersection for all modes of traffic (vehicle, pedestrian, and cyclist).

[Does the City care what residents think about construction and development?](#)
:   Yes, we genuinely want to hear your concerns and help you understand what's happening in your area! Your feedback helps us improve how we communicate and can inform future planning decisions. The City often promotes upcoming meetings and opportunities to share your opinion through various channels. Find where to [subscribe or follow City channels](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1349/Subscribe-follow-stay-informed).

/FAQ.aspx
